mgmt_bio.text: Luke Miels is an Australian pharmaceutical executive who became chief executive officer of GSK plc and joined its board on 1 January 2026, following his appointment as CEO designate in September 2025, having joined GSK in 2017 as Chief Commercial Officer. In that commercial role he had worldwide responsibility for medicines and vaccines and was instrumental in building GSK's specialty medicines portfolio, notably in oncology and respiratory. He began his career at AstraZeneca, later held senior roles at Sanofi-Aventis in the United States and Asia, worked in Roche's Asia-Pacific division, and served as executive vice president of AstraZeneca's European business. He holds a biology degree from Flinders University in Adelaide and an MBA from Macquarie University, Sydney. As CEO he is tasked with delivering GSK's sales target of more than 40 billion pounds by 2031.

sentences.quote:
Walmsley will step down from GSK's board at the end of the year but will remain with GSK until her notice period ends on September 30, 2026.

Miels will assume full responsibilities as chief executive on January 1.
sentences.text: Luke Miels became chief executive and joined the board on 1 January 2026, succeeding Emma Walmsley, who had led GSK since April 2017; she stepped down from the board at the end of 2025 but remained with the company until her notice period ended on 30 September 2026.

Miels expanded the leadership team, renamed the Executive Committee, with new appointees including Nina Mojas as President, Global Product Strategy, Maya Martinez-Davis, Lynn Baxter, Mike Crichton and Mondher Mahjoubi as Chief Patient Officer, while his former chief commercial officer role was not backfilled.
Roy Jakobs was appointed a non-executive director effective 13 July 2026.

sentences.text: Luke Miels became chief executive on 1 January 2026 after a board process that considered internal and external candidates, having joined GSK in 2017 as chief commercial officer overseeing the global medicines and vaccines portfolio.

sentences.quote: Q2 2026 sales grew 5% at constant exchange rates to GBP 8.4bn, with core operating profit up 7% to GBP 2.8bn
sentences.text: Execution so far has tracked guidance: Q2 2026 sales rose 5% to GBP 8.4bn with core operating profit up 7%, and full-year guidance was pointed to the upper half of the 3-5% turnover range, with the 2031 outlook of over GBP 40bn reaffirmed.

On capital allocation, the Accelerate Growth programme targets GBP 1.9bn of annual savings by 2029, redirected to late-stage R&D, alongside an $11bn Nuvalent acquisition in oncology and a 70p full-year dividend.
Returns on that reinvestment remain unproven.

sentences.text: The longer-term case rests on sales of more than 40 billion pounds by 2031 and an operating margin stable to improving through the dolutegravir loss-of-exclusivity period of 2028 to 2030.

sentences.quote: GSK now also expects to start 20+ phase III trials in 2026 (previously 10).

sentences.quote: The company declared a fourth-quarter dividend of 18p, taking the full-year payout to 66p, with 70p targeted for 2026. GSK has executed GBP 1.4 billion of its GBP 2 billion share buyback programme to date.

thesis_pillars.text: The longer-term case rests on sales of more than 40 billion pounds by 2031 and an operating margin stable to improving through the dolutegravir loss-of-exclusivity period of 2028 to 2030. R&D acceleration is central, with over 20 phase III trial starts planned in 2026. Cost discipline and returns support the thesis via the Accelerate Growth plan targeting 1.9 billion pounds of annual savings by 2029, largely reinvested in the late-stage pipeline, alongside a 66p 2025 dividend, 70p targeted for 2026, and a 2 billion pound buyback.
